title: [IELTS INSIGHTS] - A traditional and modern two-storey Japanese house
prompt: The plans below show a traditional and modern two-storey Japanese house. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The floor plans illustrate the interior of a traditional two-storey Japanese house and its modern counterpart.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there are several differences between the layouts of the houses, as the modern design is mostly open plan downstairs and there are more rooms upstairs. In both modern and traditional houses, the so-called traditional rooms with sliding doors double as living areas and bedrooms, with foldaway futon beds which are stored in cupboards when not in use.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking first at the ground floor, the entrance in the lower right corner of the traditional layout opens into a hallway along the right side of the building, with a bathroom and a kitchen on the left, both with their own separate spaces and doors. At the other end and along the shorter side is a traditional Japanese bedroom with a sliding door and a small cupboard, fitted with a kind of straw mat flooring called tatami. In the modern layout, the corresponding bedroom is reoriented along the longer side of the house and replaces the kitchen. Meanwhile, the original bathroom has been replaced by an open kitchen space, and the remaining space on this floor serves as a common living and dining area.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Upstairs, the traditional layout features two tatami bedrooms with sliding doors, each with its own futon cupboard. In the contemporary layout, by contrast, there are two smaller bedrooms instead of one large one at the top of the floor plan, all with modern western-style beds. On the opposite side, what originally was the other bedroom is now a master bedroom with a private bathroom, and a separate bathroom opposite the stairs.
